draft.title: Lewin's three-step model
card: Unfreeze
prepare staff to let go of old ways. Managers explain why change is needed so people see the old way no longer works.
Change
the new ways are put in place, such as new systems, roles or processes. Staff learn and begin to use them.
Refreeze
the new ways are made the normal way of working, so they stick. This can be done with policies, training and rewards.
Without refreezing, staff may drift back to old habits.
draft.remember: Unfreeze the old, make the change, then refreeze so the new ways stick.

a.q: Which step is a manager taking when she updates job descriptions and training so a new system becomes standard practice?
a.why: Making the new way the normal way of working is refreezing. Change is the tempting wrong answer, but that step is when the new system is first put in place and learnt.
a.clue: The new way is already in use. Now it must last.

b.q: Bayside Dental brings in digital booking. Staff use it for a month, then go back to paper because nothing was done to lock in the new way. Which step was most likely missed?
b.why: Staff did use the new system, so the change step happened. They drifted back because the new way was never made the normal way, which is the refreeze step.
b.clue: The change happened. What failed was making it last.

problems.detail: The stem says staff went back to paper 'because nothing was done to lock in the new way'. This nearly restates the card's definition of refreezing, so a student can match words instead of applying the model.

check.summary: The card and answers are accurate, and Refreeze is the single right answer to both questions. Question b's stem ('nothing was done to lock in the new way') largely gives the answer away.

proposal.title: Lewin's three-step change model
card: Unfreeze
prepare staff to let go of old ways. Managers explain why change is needed so people see the old way no longer works.
Change
the new ways are put in place, such as new systems, roles or processes. Staff learn and begin to use them.
Refreeze
the new ways are made the normal way of working, so they stick. This can be done with policies, training and rewards.
The steps happen in that order. Without refreezing, staff may drift back to old habits.
proposal.remember: Unfreeze the old, make the change, then refreeze so the new ways stick.

a.q: Which step is a manager taking when she updates job descriptions and training so a new system becomes standard practice?
a.why: Making the new way the normal way of working is refreezing. Change is the tempting wrong answer, but that step is when the new system is first put in place and learnt.
a.clue: The new way is already in use. Now it must last.

b.q: Bayside Dental trains staff in digital booking, and they use it for a month. The manager then moves to another project, the paper diary stays at reception, and by month three staff are back on paper. Which step was weakest?
b.why: Staff were trained and used the system for a month, so the unfreeze and change steps worked. No policy, follow-up or reward made it the normal way of working, so staff drifted back. That is a weak refreeze step.
b.clue: Staff did use the new system for a whole month.
